annotation.title_clean: DOCTRINAL-LEGAL AND ETHICAL PROBLEMS OF DEVELOPING AND APPLYING ROBOTIC TECHNOLOGIES AND ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE SYSTEMS (USING AUTONOMOUS UNMANNED UNDERWATER VEHICLES)
annotation.title_en: Doctrinal-Legal and Ethical Problems of Developing and Applying Robotic Technologies and Artificial Intelligence Systems (Using Autonomous Unmanned Underwater Vehicles)
annotation.authors_or_issuer: Baranov, P.; Mamychev, A.; Mordovtsev, A.; Danilyan, O.G.; Dzeban, A.P.
annotation.venue: Visnyk of the National Academy of Managerial Staff of Culture and Arts (Вісник Національної академії керівних кадрів культури і мистецтв), No. 2
named_instruments_referenced: EU Civil Law Rules on Robotics 2017
annotation.summary_en: Journal article systematizing doctrinal, legal and ethical problems in regulating robotics and AI, using autonomous unmanned underwater vehicles (civil and military) as the case. It argues existing legal models are inadequate and calls for a new legal concept, deontological codes and international standards, noting competition among states to set them.
key_provisions_or_claims: No general legal concept or ethical coding exists for autonomous underwater vehicles at national or international level.
Adapting existing regulatory models to robotics and AI is judged ineffective.
Calls for an advanced legal modeling concept, common doctrine and standardization before legislative reform.
States that build effective legal models can shape international legal standards.
Cites the EU's October 2017 decision to develop a European legal and ethical concept for robotics and AI.
